issue_context.title: Bluesound integration not listing additional players on the same host
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a  Monitor Audio IMS-4 (which is a re-skinned NAD CI 580v2). This is a rackmount streamer that has four BluOs zones exposed from one host.

Each of the four zones exposes its HTTP API over a different port: `11000`, `11010`, `11020`, and `11030` respectively.

I've configured my HA with the config (see below)

However only the media_player.bathroom entity appears in home assistant, the other three do not appear.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.9.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Bluesound

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bluesound/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
media_player:  
  - platform: bluesound
    hosts:
      - host: 10.9.4.15
        port: 11000
        name: Bathroom
      - host: 10.9.4.15
        port: 11010
        name: WC
      - host: 10.9.4.15
        port: 11020
        name: Dining
      - host: 10.9.4.15
        port: 11030
        name: Kitchen
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing in the logs related to bluesound/media player.
```


### Additional information

I can confirm using `curl` that the above host:port combinations are correct and the API is available for each zone.
comments:
[bluesound documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bluesound)
[bluesound source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/bluesound)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
Workaround: I have a local DNS server. So I created 4 different hostnames (e.g., zone1.mydomain.com ... zone4.mydomain.com) and used these domain names in the host field. This causes all 4 zones to appear as media player entities.

Is there some sort of de-dupping happening on the `CONF_HOST` key? I don't see it in the source code for this integration, could it be happening in the code that parses and loads the yaml config?



```yaml
media_player:  
  - platform: bluesound
    hosts:
      - host: bathroom.mydomain.com
        port: 11000
        name: Bathroom
      - host: wc.mydomain.com
        port: 11010
        name: WC
      - host: dining.mydomain.com
        port: 11020
        name: Dining
      - host: kitchen.mydomain.com
        port: 11030
        name: Kitchen
```
Ok, spoke to soon. 

Using the hostname method outlined previously only detection of the device works, controlling and joining/unjoining does not work.

Somewhere along the way the hostnames seem to be resolved into their ip addreses, and then the bluesound integration compares the hostnames by ip address.

I am seeing log lines like the following when trying to call `service.join`

```
2021-10-05 18:01:56 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.bluesound.media_player] Master not found 10.9.4.15
2021-10-05 18:01:56 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.bluesound.media_player] Master not found 10.9.4.15
```
(note, that the ip address appears no where in my config)

[This section of code](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/3c074ab865855bd950f771161c2b02e4fb5d3f2a/homeassistant/components/bluesound/media_player.py#L263-L281) is comparing the `host` values. If these values have been resolved to the ip address, then indeed it won't work.

Could I please attract the attention of a proper home-assistant developer who can speak as to how the `CONF_HOST` and `CONF_HOSTS` config values work and how/if hostnames are resolved into ip addreses?

review_comments:
This is ok for now. For the future we should preferably refactor the integration to not store the entities in hass.data but just store a set of known ids for added players. Also refactor the custom service registration to use our entity service helper. And also use our standard join / unjoin media player interface.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/dev_101_services#entity-services

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/media-player#grouping-player-entities-together

And of course, this integration will need a 3rd party library for the device interface for us to accept any major changes.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/creating_component_code_review#4-communication-with-devicesservices

Yeah, I've been planning for two years to refactor this into a seperate library. Hopefully I can find the time for it soon enough. They have also released documentation of the API which will make it easier to make a library that meets my own requirements :)
